shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A to go from 1B to 2B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C — reducing variety and giving up a good I equally value with no gain in diversity. Current balanced bundle (1,1,1) is better than an unbalanced one.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away B for A would just shift the imbalance (2 A, 0 B, 1 C) without improving variety - it would make my holdings less balanced, which reduces utility given my preference for variety.

Current inventory is balanced at 1-1-1. Trading away my only B for 2 A would make me have 3A/0B/1C, creating a strong imbalance and losing all variety in B, which is less desirable under my preference for variety.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating an imbalanced bundle (2,1,0->2,0,1... actually B=2,C=0), which reduces variety and thus utility. Since I value variety, I should not deplete a good to zero.

I currently have equal quantities (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my B for their C would just swap which good I have less of, resulting in the same variety (1,0,2) instead of (1,1,1) - actually it would make me 1 A, 0 B, 2 C, which is less balanced than my current even split. This decreases variety, so I reject.

Currently I have 1 each of A, B, C - a perfectly even bundle. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1A, 0B, 3C, which is much less diverse and less valuable given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep balance or find a trade that doesn't zero out a good.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:2, so B is my scarcest good. Trading 1 A (of which I have 2) for 1 B (of which I have 0) moves me toward a more balanced, higher-variety bundle (A:1, B:1, C:2), which increases my utility given diminishing value on abundant goods.

A fairer trade would be 1C for 1B to balance my bundle toward A2,B1,C1. I'll reject this and counter for a 1:1 trade instead.
